traceability.evidence: Story file docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md defines requirements REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG, REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES, REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION, REQ-CONSISTENCY, and REQ-PATTERN-TESTING, and includes concrete configuration examples using storyPathPattern, requirementIdPattern, storyPathExample, and requirementIdExample.,tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts explicitly declares support for docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md and related requirements via @story and @req annotations in the header comment. It contains many tests whose names and expectations map directly to this story’s requirements, including: [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY-FLAT], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ-FLAT], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH-FLAT], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT], [REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG], and [REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES]. All these tests pass under `npm test`.,Core functionality (configurable patterns): src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts defines AnnotationRuleOptions with both nested and flat configuration options: `story?.pattern`, `req?.pattern`, and shorthand `storyPathPattern`, `requirementIdPattern`, `storyPathExample`, `requirementIdExample`. resolveOptions() reads these options, resolves them into ResolvedAnnotationOptions (storyPattern, storyExample, reqPattern, reqExample), and stores them in a shared resolvedDefaults cache. valid-annotation-format rule’s create() uses resolveOptions() and passes the resolved options into the validators, so configured patterns are actually used.,Backward compatibility and defaults: valid-annotation-options.ts provides getDefaultStoryPattern(), getDefaultStoryExample(), getDefaultReqPattern(), and getDefaultReqExample() functions and initializes resolvedDefaults with these defaults. resolvePattern() returns the provided defaultPattern when neither nestedPattern nor flatPattern is a string. resolveOptions() uses these helpers so that if no custom patterns are supplied, the rule behavior falls back to the original hard-coded patterns. Tests such as basic valid/invalid cases for @story/@req in valid-annotation-format.test.ts (e.g., without options) still use the original docs/stories/... and REQ-* shapes and pass, confirming backward compatibility.,Regex validation and safe fallback: valid-annotation-options.ts implements resolvePattern(), which attempts `new RegExp(effective.value)` inside a try/catch. On failure it pushes a configuration error message built by buildInvalidRegexError(field, pattern) into the global optionErrors array and returns the defaultPattern, thereby satisfying REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION and REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT. valid-annotation-format.ts’s create() reads these optionErrors via getOptionErrors() and, in the Program listener, reports each as a diagnostic with messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration". Tests in valid-annotation-format.test.ts named “[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] invalid storyPathPattern falls back to default behavior”, “[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] invalid requirementIdPattern falls back to default behavior”, and the corresponding *-FLAT variants assert both the configuration error messages and the continued use of default examples and auto-fix behavior, confirming correct regex validation and safe fallback.,Error messages and examples: valid-annotation-options.resolveExample() prefers nested example strings over flat ones, and falls back to the default example when neither is provided (REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT). src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts uses the resolved options in buildStoryErrorMessage() and buildReqErrorMessage(), basing error text on options.storyExample / options.reqExample and defaulting to STORY_EXAMPLE_PATH or getDefaultReqExample() when needed. Tests in valid-annotation-format.test.ts explicitly exercise this: “[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES] custom story example appears in error message”, “[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES] custom requirement example appears in error message”, “[REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES] nested story example text overrides flat storyPathExample in error messages”, and “[REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES] nested req example text overrides flat requirementIdExample in error messages” all assert that the error detail strings contain the expected custom examples and that nested examples override flat ones.,ESLint rule schema and configuration: valid-annotation-options.getRuleSchema() returns a JSON Schema array with a single object describing the rule options: `story` and `req` objects (each with string properties `pattern` and `example` and additionalProperties: false) plus top-level `storyPathPattern`, `storyPathExample`, `requirementIdPattern`, and `requirementIdExample` string properties, and overall `additionalProperties: false`. src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts sets `schema: getRuleSchema()` in its meta, so ESLint uses this schema for configuration validation, satisfying REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION and the “Quality Standards” acceptance criterion that the rule follows ESLint schema best practices.,Validation behavior uses configured patterns: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-validators.ts consumes the ResolvedAnnotationOptions produced by resolveOptions(). validateStoryAnnotation() tests `options.storyPattern` against the collapsed story path and uses buildStoryErrorMessage(options) when invalid, and validateReqAnnotation() tests `options.reqPattern` and uses buildReqErrorMessage(options). Because storyPattern and reqPattern are wired to either default or user-defined regexes, all story and requirement format validation honors the custom patterns, fulfilling REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG and REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION.,Rule-level configuration error reporting: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts defines a new messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration" specifically tied to docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md with requirements REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION and REQ-BACKWARD-COMP, and uses it in the Program listener to surface regex configuration errors collected during resolveOptions(). Tests in valid-annotation-format.test.ts assert that this messageId is produced with the correct details when patterns such as "[unclosed" or "(unclosed" are provided both in nested and flat options.,Integration and consistency with valid-story-reference: The default story path regex in valid-annotation-options.getDefaultStoryPattern() is `^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$`, which is consistent with the valid-story-reference rule’s expectations: src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts uses default storyDirectories ["docs/stories", "stories"] and requires the `.story.md` extension by default. Tests in tests/rules/valid-story-reference.test.ts (e.g., “[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] honors custom storyDirectories using docs/stories”, “[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] allowAbsolutePaths accepts existing absolute .story.md inside project”, and “[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS] requireStoryExtension=false accepts existing .md story file”) demonstrate that valid-story-reference has its own configurable resolution layer (storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension). Since valid-annotation-format controls regex format only and defaults to docs/stories/*.story.md, and valid-story-reference controls existence and directories with matching defaults, they work together without conflict, satisfying the story’s “Integration” and REQ-CONSISTENCY intent.,Testing coverage for pattern configuration and edge cases: tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts contains a comprehensive matrix of valid and invalid cases using both nested and flat pattern configs, including: accepting custom story/req patterns (`[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY]`, `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ]`, `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH]`, and their flat equivalents), verifying example messages (`[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES]`, `[REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES]`), verifying precedence of nested over flat (`[REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG]` tests for precedence of nested pattern/example over flat), and invalid regex fallback behavior (`[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK]`, `[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT]`). These tests collectively satisfy REQ-PATTERN-TESTING and demonstrate that all acceptance criteria around configuration behavior, error handling, and messaging are functionally verified.,Documentation/examples: The story file docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md itself includes a “Use Case Examples” section with concrete ESLint configuration snippets showing different directory structures (custom storyPathPattern and storyPathExample), different requirement ID prefixes (custom requirementIdPattern and requirementIdExample), and custom story file formats. These examples directly use the new options `storyPathPattern`, `requirementIdPattern`, `storyPathExample`, and `requirementIdExample`, fulfilling the “Documentation” acceptance criterion for clear configuration examples.,Global test status: Running `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose` executed all Jest test suites, including tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts. The output shows that all 38 test suites and all 288 tests passed with no failures, confirming that the implementation and tests for this story are green in the current codebase.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are fully implemented and verified. The valid-annotation-format rule now supports both nested and flat configuration for story and requirement patterns and examples, validates user-supplied regex patterns with clear configuration error reporting, falls back safely to default behavior when patterns are invalid or absent, and integrates cleanly with existing valid-story-reference behavior through consistent defaults. Comprehensive unit tests cover configurable patterns, message examples, precedence rules, and invalid pattern fallback, and documentation/examples are present in the story file itself. Therefore this story is considered PASSED.
